tts_summary:
Here is your midday market update for Monday, September 21st.

Stocks are broadly higher but the rally is narrow. The Nasdaq is up 153 basis points while the equal-weight S&P is up just 30 basis points — that divergence tells you everything about what is driving this market today. Two themes dominate: AI euphoria around Meta Muse and falling oil prices after Trump backed off Houthi airstrikes at the last minute Sunday night.

On the macro side, Treasuries have a modest bid with yields down 1 to 3 basis points across the curve. Oil is slumping roughly 400 basis points, dropping below 100 dollars a barrel, as diplomatic optimism builds ahead of the UN General Assembly this week. Trump has indicated he would be open to meeting with Iran's president, and markets are pricing in some probability of Middle East de-escalation. That said, the situation remains fragile — Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia escalated sharply over the weekend, Iran is issuing warnings, and the State Department is cautioning American citizens about unforeseen escalation risk.

Now the key company stories.

Meta is one of the top names in the entire market today. The Meta Muse AI assistant is generating strong early demand signals and traders are front-running Zuckerberg's keynote at the Connect Conference Wednesday night. The read-through is significant: agentic AI is much more compute-intensive than prior AI iterations, and that is directly lifting CPU makers. AMD and Intel are both surging on this thesis — if Muse breaks agentic AI into the mainstream consumer market, the demand uplift for CPUs could be substantial.

On the negative side, HP Inc. is sliding after saying PC unit volumes are expected to fall roughly 5% in calendar 2027. That is a meaningful cautious data point for the PC cycle.

Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery are both jumping after Paramount reached a settlement with state attorneys general, clearing the main legal obstacle to their merger. Paramount will reportedly preserve CNN's editorial independence and divest some cable channels including Comedy Central. The overhang is lifted.

Novo Nordisk is underperforming after failing to provide sufficiently granular financial targets at its analyst meeting today — investors wanted more and did not get it.

Oracle remains a concern after a negative report highlighted that debt tied to its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico is struggling to find buyers, adding to broader worries about Big Tech off-balance-sheet AI liabilities, which are up roughly 300 billion dollars in just the last twelve months.

In the potash space, CF Industries, Mosaic, and Nutrien are all getting hit after Trump said the US is near a massive supply deal with Belarus at prices substantially below current Canadian potash rates. That is a direct pricing threat to the sector.

Directionally, the setup leans bullish intraday but watch the breadth problem closely. The rally is being carried by a handful of mega-cap AI names. Wednesday night's Meta keynote is the next major catalyst. Geopolitical headlines out of the UN General Assembly are the key macro wildcard in either direction.
